Target Heart Rate

Training zones

Measurement System Units

Step 1 of 2

What is Target Heart Rate?

Your target heart rate is a specific beats-per-minute (BPM) range you should aim for during cardiovascular exercise to achieve specific results, like fat burning or aerobic endurance.

How to Use This Calculator

  1. Enter your age and your resting heart rate (taken right after waking up).
  2. View your personalized heart rate zones.
  3. Use a fitness tracker or smartwatch to stay in your desired zone during workouts.

How We Calculate Target Heart Rate

We use the Karvonen method, which factors in your resting heart rate to find your Heart Rate Reserve (HRR), combined with the Tanaka formula (208 - 0.7 × age) for Maximum Heart Rate.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is the best zone for fat burning?

Zone 2 (60-70% of maximum HR) burns the highest percentage of calories from fat, making it ideal for steady-state cardio.

How do I measure my resting heart rate?

Measure your pulse for 60 seconds immediately after waking up naturally in the morning, while still lying in bed.

Is the '220 minus age' formula accurate?

The older '220 minus age' formula is a rough estimate but is often inaccurate. We use the updated Tanaka formula which research shows is more precise.

Why is my heart rate higher than normal during exercise?

Heat, humidity, dehydration, caffeine, and lack of sleep can all elevate your heart rate higher than normal for a given effort level.
